ca_little_pinnacle_aka_mini_buttress.blurb: Little Pinnacle is a small formation in Pine Creek Canyon above Bishop, on the Eastern Sierra side, at roughly 7,200 feet. It sits within the Scheelite Canyon side drainage, the canyon's most visited arm, just upstream from the Gecko Wall, and has climbing on three separate faces. Eight sport routes make up the tally, and the grades are mostly 5.10 with a single 5.8, a pair of 5.11s and one 5.12, so it suits a climber warming up on mid-grade bolted lines. Faces of granodiorite take the shade through the afternoon, which helps on warm days.

ca_dike_walk_wall.blurb: Dike Walk Wall is one of the walls inside Keepers Cove, a High Desert cove near Apple Valley at about 3,100 feet. It is a tall formation with a handful of good lines on it, and it has eight routes: six bolted and two trad. Difficulty stays moderate to middling, with three routes at 5.7, one at 5.9 and four in the 5.10 range, which makes it a sensible stop for a leader stepping up from easy sport climbing. The rock is monzogranite.

ca_el_dorado.blurb: El Dorado is a small outcrop on Cabrillo Peak (Cerro Cabrillo) in Morro Bay State Park, on California's Central Coast near San Luis Obispo. It is the closest rock to Rockland and a notch harder than that neighbor, with the same slick dacite. Eight routes are spread across three styles: three sport lines, three top-rope problems and two trad climbs. Grades run from 5.5 up to 5.12, with a good number of beginner and low-intermediate options alongside a few hard bolted leads, so it works for a mixed group.

ca_mad_cow_wall.blurb: Mad Cow Wall is a compact granodiorite face in the Central Pinnacles of Holcomb Valley, in the mountains north of Big Bear Lake at around 7,550 feet. It faces east, so it takes the morning sun and falls into shade after midday. The wall stands high enough off the trail that it is easy to overlook, and reaching the base involves a short scramble. It has eight routes: four sport, three trad and one top-rope. Most fall at 5.10, with one 5.8 and two 5.11s.

ca_hinterland_wall.blurb: Hinterland Wall belongs to The Hinterland, a small cluster of cliffs in the Tahquitz and Suicide Rocks area of the San Jacinto Mountains, at close to 7,700 feet. The wall is known for splitter cracks, and its eight routes are protected with a trad rack. Grades start at 5.7 and top out in the 5.11 range, with several around 5.9 and 5.10. A gully of further crack climbs, with about fourteen more routes, sits just above the wall for those wanting a longer day in the same spot. The rock is tonalite.
